summary: Phase-based zero-downtime rename: expand adds customer_note column and backfills note values, then creates a PostgreSQL bidirectional trigger to keep note and customer_note synchronized during the overlap; deploy_new starts new version with state_only migration; retire_old retires old version; contract drops trigger and note column, leaving customer_note as the sole note column.
write_consistency: Old version writes to column note, new version writes to customer_note. A PostgreSQL trigger fires after each INSERT and UPDATE on account_user, ensuring that if note changes, customer_note is set to the new note value, and if customer_note changes, note is set to the new customer_note value. This maintains column parity at all times, so reads from either version return the most recently written value.
revision_notes: Root cause of previous failures: no mechanism to synchronize note and customer_note columns after deploy_new, causing divergent values and failed cross-version read checks. This plan adds a bidirectional UPDATE trigger in the expand stage to maintain column consistency throughout the overlap.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill initial values, and create sync trigger
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note_trig AFTER UPDATE OR INSERT ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Retire old version; old app no longer serves traffic
Drop trigger and note column after old version retired
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
